_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 25 (Keturah; Abraham's death; Ishmael's lineage; Esau & Jacob). Saadia-specific moves: v.16 שריף = 'noble' for נשיא; v.20 'פדאן ארם' transliterated; v.22 'תלתמס עלמא מן ענד אללה' = 'to seek knowledge from God' (Saadia's interpretive gloss for לדרש את ה' — soft 'to seek instruction from God'); v.27 'סאדגא' = 'simple/innocent' for תם; v.30 אדום=אלאחמרי 'the red one' (Saadia: nickname etymology).

translations.1: Then Abraham repeated, and took a wife whose name was Keturah.
translations.2: And she bore him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Yishbaq, and Shuah.
translations.3: And Yokshan begot Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translations.4: And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah — all these were sons of Keturah.
translations.5: And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
translations.6: And to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he was still alive, eastward — to the land of the east.
translations.7: And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life that he lived — a hundred and seventy-five years.
translations.8: Then Abraham expired and died — in a good old age, an old man satisfied with years — and he was gathered to his people.
translations.9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of the doubled field, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is over against Mamre,
translations.10: the field which Abraham had bought from the sons of Heth — there Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
translations.11: And it was after the death of Abraham, that God blessed Isaac his son; and Isaac settled by the Well of the Living One who Sees.
translations.12: And this is the exposition of the offspring of Ishmael the son of Abraham — whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
translations.13: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their offspring: Nebayot the firstborn of Ishmael, and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
translations.14: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
translations.15: Hadad, and Tema, Yetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translations.16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, in their settlements and their citadels — twelve noble ones according to their nations.
translations.17: And these are the years of Ishmael's life — a hundred and thirty-seven years; and he expired and died, and was gathered to his people.
translations.18: And they dwelt from Zawila (Havilah) to al-Ghafar (Shur), which is over against Egypt, as you come to Mosul (Asshur); in the presence of all his brothers did he settle.
translations.19: And this is the exposition of the offspring of Isaac son of Abraham — after Abraham had singled out Isaac from his children.
translations.20: And when Isaac was a son of forty years, he took Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean, from Paddan-Aram, sister of Laban the Aramean — and she became his wife.
translations.21: Then Isaac entreated God concerning his wife, for she was barren; and God granted his entreaty, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
translations.22: And the children jostled in her womb; and she said: 'If I had known the matter were thus, I would not have sought it.' And she went to seek knowledge from God.
translations.23: And God said to her: 'Behold, the fathers of two nations are in your womb; and two factions from your bowels shall be separated; and the one shall be stronger than the other; and the elder shall serve the younger.'
translations.24: And when her days were completed for bearing — behold, there were twins in her womb.
translations.25: And the first came forth ruddy, all of him like a mantle of hair; and they named him Esau.
translations.26: And after that came forth his brother, and his hand was grasping Esau's heel; and he named him Jacob. And Isaac was a son of sixty years when they were born.
translations.27: And when the two youths grew up, Esau was a man knowing of hunting, a man of the wilderness; and Jacob was a simple man, dwelling in tents.
translations.28: And Isaac loved Esau for his knowing of hunting; but Rebekah loved Jacob.
translations.29: Then Jacob cooked a stew; and Esau came in from the wilderness, and he was faint.
translations.30: And he said to Jacob: 'Feed me of this red [stuff] — for I am faint.' Therefore he was called The Red One (Edom).
translations.31: And Jacob said: 'Sell to me today your birthright.'
translations.32: Esau said: 'Behold, I am going to die — and what is a birthright to me?'
translations.33: He said to him: 'Swear to me.' And he swore to him, and sold him his birthright.
translations.34: And Jacob gave him bread and a stew of lentils; and he ate, and drank, and rose, and went away. And Esau despised the birthright.
